lines.content: PlayStation -1 is a lightweight collection of keyboard-driven command-line games for quick breaks in the terminal. The project keeps the experience simple: choose a game, play without leaving the shell, and return to the menu when you are finished.
The minimum viable product contains one Wordle-style word-guessing game. Players receive feedback after each guess and can complete a short game session entirely from the command line.
Prerequisites: JDK 25 (use the exact version), update Intellij to the most recent version.

1. **Ensure Intellij JDK 25 is defined as an SDK**, as described [here](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/sdk.html#set-up-jdk) -- this step is not needed if you have used JDK 25 in a previous Intellij project.
1. **Import the project _as a Gradle project_**, as described [here](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/intellijImportGradleProject.html).

1. **Verify the setup**: After importing, run the application from IntelliJ or execute `./gradlew run` (macOS/Linux) or `gradlew.bat run` (Windows) in the project folder. A successful run starts the command-line application.

**Warning:** Keep the `src\main\java` folder as the root folder for Java files (i.e., don't rename those folders or move Java files to another folder outside of this folder path), as this is the default location some tools (e.g., Gradle) expect to find Java files.

handled as one input followed by one output. The application does not use

PlayStation -1 is a keyboard-first command-line arcade for people who enjoy quick, self-contained games without leaving the terminal. It is designed for short breaks: start a game with one command, play for as long as you like, and return to the menu when you are done.

Version 1.0 provides a terminal menu and a data-driven game catalogue featuring the **calculator** game. Players can view help and game information, launch the game, solve randomly generated arithmetic problems, receive immediate feedback, and see a session summary when they quit. All interaction is through the keyboard, and scores last for the current session only.
1. Ensure that you have Java 25 or above installed.
